text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week slide of 14%, as oil prices weakened and refinery margins compressed. US crude dropped to $82.24 per barrel while refineries ran at 95.7% capacity—near maximum—with gasoline and diesel inventories rising, a signal that demand isn't keeping pace with supply. When refineries are already running flat out and product stockpiles are building, there's little room for profitability to expand.

The broader headwind is energy transition risk. Climate talks collapsed over the weekend without committing fossil fuels to phase-out language, which should theoretically be bullish for oil; instead, the market seems focused on longer-term uncertainty around energy demand as quantum computing and AI infrastructure push toward alternative energy solutions. For a refiner whose earnings depend on the spread between crude costs and refined product prices, that combination of near-term margin pressure and longer-term demand concerns has weighed on the stock.
